name: BhoomiSetu
tagline: A land-survey readiness assistant that lines up what each land record says, flags where they disagree, and shows the source for every number.
problem: Preparing for a land survey in Bihar can mean reconstructing one case from historical Khatiyan records, current Jamabandi entries, survey Parcha data, parcel maps and family context. The hard part for a citizen is knowing what evidence exists, what agrees and what needs review. BhoomiSetu demonstrates that evidence workflow on synthetic data without making legal or ownership decisions.
how: A case is created from district, circle, mauza, Khata and Khesra details, or the preloaded synthetic Demo Case 001 is opened.
Each synthetic document can be inspected as source text, and optional Gemini or OpenAI extraction suggests structured fields that must pass schema, evidence-span and grounding checks.
Deterministic verification code, not an LLM, compares identifiers and areas and returns PASS, POTENTIAL_ISSUE or INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE with source references.
Parcel Intelligence computes the mapped area from synthetic GeoJSON with Turf and compares historical, survey and mapped areas.
A verification result can be anchored with a SHA-256 hash and checked on a public integrity page without logging in.
Official-style record lookup and two-date Earth Observation add context, and the Next Action page gives one practical preparation step.
features: Case dashboard with area gap, holder name and field match summaries
Document evidence view with source text and extraction traceability
Deterministic area and family-context verification with explicit insufficient-evidence outcomes
Three-way area comparison: historical 1.20 acre, survey 1.02 acre and mapped 1.0243 acre for the hero case
Signed verification anchors with a public integrity verifier page
Synthetic official-record lookup and Earth Observation context behind provider boundaries
Guided next action, timeline and local review packet preparation
1-click sample fill on the create case form
ai: Optional Gemini or OpenAI extraction suggests structured facts from synthetic document text, validated with Zod schemas, evidence spans and semantic grounding checks.
Without a configured provider, extraction returns a safe unavailable state and the rest of the flow still works.
No LLM decides discrepancies or legal outcomes; verification is rule-based.

stack.frontend: Next.js 16, React 19, TypeScript, MapLibre GL, cobe
stack.backend: Next.js route handlers with case, verification, parcel, anchor and review packet services
stack.data: Node SQLite locally; Postgres or Supabase adapter when DATABASE_URL is set; synthetic fixtures and GeoJSON; Turf for area
stack.ai: Optional Gemini (@google/genai) or OpenAI extraction with Zod validation

notes: Ran locally as a production build with the default local SQLite database and the repo's synthetic demo data; no code changes. No AI key was set, so the AI extraction step was not run and its output is not shown. The OpenStreetMap basemap tiles were blocked by the network sandbox, so the parcel map shows the synthetic boundary with the app's own Map background unavailable notice. The sample case fill, anchor creation and record search were done in the real UI; the local SQLite file was restored afterwards.
